newsitem.title: POLAND: Zloty eyes more downside after rate rise jump.
newsitem.headline: Zloty eyes more downside after rate rise jump.

text.p: The Polish zloty, which lost some 0.3 points against its basket on Wednesday, may be in for more loses over the next few days amid a strong U.S. dollar and continued large orders from importers, dealers said.
Over the last week the zloty jumped about one point to highs at 0.5 percent below parity on Monday after official interest rates were increased, but has lost ground since.
"This downtrend for the zloty may be sustained and the Polish unit could fall to around -1.0 to -1.2 percent from parity," said Jaroslaw Dryjski, dealer at Bank Slaski SA.
The zloty closed at -0.86/-0.94 percent from the trading band centre, against Tuesday's -0.66/-0.71 percent.
It closed at 3.5020/60 to the dollar, against 3.4840/55 on Tuesday and at 1.8545/60 to the mark, against 1.8550/65.

Dealers said Tuesday's threat by the co-ruling Peasant Party (PSL) that it would seek to oust the ex-communist premier unless farming policy demands were met represented largely an attempt to boost its popularity before the polls.
"The rift will definitely not help the zloty, but should not harm it, either. This seems to be a regular election fight," Dryjski said.
On the money market one-day deposits slipped by another half point as the central bank refrained from any open market operations, which would have drained the cash-heavy market, dealers said.
Overnight rates closed at 22.80/23.30 percent against Tuesday's 23.30/24.00 percent. Tommorow/next were at 22.80/23.30 percent against 23.35/23.90 percent.
The finance ministry cut the minimum prices of its 15-percent two-year bond to 86.60 zlotys from 89.67 and of its 12-percent five-year bond to 75.40 zlotys from 79.15.
